title: Turning — Who were they to you?

rows.label: Someone under your guidance. They looked up to you with admiration and aspired to be more like you. They may have been an apprentice, a student, a younger sibling, etc.
Someone you hated. You may or may not have had a pleasant relationship in the past, but in the present, you never saw eye to eye. They may have been a rival, a boss, an ex, etc.
A service provider. You used to be their client. They may have been a plumber, therapist, doctor, waiter, etc.
A colleague or contact. Your relationship was based on mutual academic or professional background. They may have been a classmate, a coworker, a business contact, etc.

An acquaintance. You knew each other by name and even said hi, but you never talked much. They may have been a significant other’s cousin, a friend of one of your parents, your neighbor you saw now and then, etc.
A complete stranger. You met them for the first time right before they turned you.
A mentor. They were a figure of authority and wisdom to you, like a more experienced colleague, a professor, etc.
A lover. You used to fill each other with lust and affection. They may have been a significant other, a friend with benefits, a situationship, etc.
A great friend. You could always count on each other in any situation. They may have been a roommate, a friend, a best friend, etc.
A relative. Close or distant, even in life you had blood ties. They may have been a cousin, aunt, uncle, sibling, etc.
